config_file_lookup.after_env: getpwuid(geteuid())->pw_dir checked with the plain file name (no dot/underscore variants) when HAVE_GETPWUID && HAVE_GETEUID
dotscore_macro: #define CURLRC_DOTSCORE 2 /* look for underscore-prefixed name too */
config_file_lookup.files_doc:
*~/.curlrc*

Default config file, see --config for details.
needs_manual_reading: src/tool_parsecfg.c parseconfig(): the full .curlrc / -K parsing (quoting, '-' for stdin, option:argument syntax)
src/tool_findfile.c findfile(): the withoutdot/dotscore interplay (dotscore is cleared after the first withoutdot attempt)
config_file_lookup.per_directory_check: checkhome(): with dotscore tries '.name' then '_name'; without, the name as given; first file that open()s read-only wins
config_file_lookup.withoutdot_rule: entries with without_dot=true are tried only when dotscore is set; they look for the name minus its leading dot (i.e. 'curlrc' under XDG_CONFIG_HOME or ~/.config)

doc.text: Success. The operation completed successfully according to the instructions.
Unsupported protocol. This build of curl has no support for this protocol.
Failed to initialize.
URL malformed. The syntax was not correct.
A feature or option that was needed to perform the desired request was not enabled or was explicitly disabled at build-time. To make curl able to do this, you probably need another build of libcurl.
Could not resolve proxy. The given proxy host could not be resolved.
Could not resolve host. The given remote host could not be resolved.
Failed to connect to host.
Weird server reply. The server sent data curl could not parse.

FTP access denied. The server denied login or denied access to the particular resource or directory you wanted to reach. Most often you tried to change to a directory that does not exist on the server.
FTP accept failed. While waiting for the server to connect back when an active FTP session is used, an error code was sent over the control connection or similar.
FTP weird PASS reply. curl could not parse the reply sent to the PASS request.
During an active FTP session while waiting for the server to connect back to curl, the timeout expired.
FTP weird PASV reply, curl could not parse the reply sent to the PASV request.
FTP weird 227 format. curl could not parse the 227-line the server sent.
FTP cannot use host. Could not resolve the host IP we got in the 227-line.
HTTP/2 error. A problem was detected in the HTTP2 framing layer. This is somewhat generic and can be one out of several problems, see the error message for details.
FTP could not set binary. Could not change transfer method to binary.
Partial file. Only a part of the file was transferred.
FTP could not download/access the given file, the RETR (or similar) command failed.
FTP quote error. A quote command returned error from the server.
HTTP page not retrieved. The requested URL was not found or returned another error with the HTTP error code being 400 or above. This return code only appears if --fail is used.
Write error. curl could not write data to a local file system or similar.
Failed starting the upload. For FTP, the server typically denied the STOR command.
Read error. Various reading problems.
Out of memory. A memory allocation request failed.
Operation timeout. The specified time-out period was reached according to the conditions.
FTP PORT failed. The PORT command failed. Not all FTP servers support the PORT command, try doing a transfer using PASV instead.
FTP could not use REST. The REST command failed. This command is used for resumed FTP transfers.
HTTP range error. The range "command" did not work.
HTTP post error. Internal post-request generation error.
SSL connect error. The SSL handshaking failed.
Bad download resume. Could not continue an earlier aborted download.
FILE could not read file. Failed to open the file. Permissions?
LDAP cannot bind. LDAP bind operation failed.
LDAP search failed.
Function not found. A required LDAP function was not found.
Aborted by callback. An application told curl to abort the operation.
Internal error. A function was called with a bad parameter.
Interface error. A specified outgoing interface could not be used.
Too many redirects. When following redirects, curl hit the maximum amount.
Unknown option specified to libcurl. This indicates that you passed a weird option to curl that was passed on to libcurl and rejected. Read up in the manual.
Malformed telnet option.
The server did not reply anything, which here is considered an error.
SSL crypto engine not found.
Cannot set SSL crypto engine as default.
Failed sending network data.
Failure in receiving network data.
Problem with the local certificate.
Could not use specified SSL cipher.
Peer certificate cannot be authenticated with known CA certificates.
Unrecognized transfer encoding.
Maximum file size exceeded.
Requested FTP SSL level failed.
Sending the data requires a rewind that failed.
Failed to initialize SSL Engine.
The username, password, or similar was not accepted and curl failed to log in.
File not found on TFTP server.
Permission problem on TFTP server.
Out of disk space on TFTP server.
Illegal TFTP operation.
Unknown TFTP transfer ID.
File already exists (TFTP).
No such user (TFTP).
Problem reading the SSL CA cert (path? access rights?).
The resource referenced in the URL does not exist.
An unspecified error occurred during the SSH session.
Failed to shut down the SSL connection.
Could not load CRL file, missing or wrong format (added in 7.19.0).
Issuer check failed (added in 7.19.0).
The FTP PRET command failed.
Mismatch of RTSP CSeq numbers.
Mismatch of RTSP Session Identifiers.
Unable to parse FTP file list.
FTP chunk callback reported error.
No connection available, the session is queued.
SSL public key does not match pinned public key.
Invalid SSL certificate status.
Stream error in HTTP/2 framing layer.
An API function was called from inside a callback.
An authentication function returned an error.
A problem was detected in the HTTP/3 layer. This is somewhat generic and can be one out of several problems, see the error message for details.
QUIC connection error. This error may be caused by an SSL library error. QUIC is the protocol used for HTTP/3 transfers.
Proxy handshake error.
A client-side certificate is required to complete the TLS handshake.
Poll or select returned fatal error.
A value or data field grew larger than allowed.
More error codes might appear here in future releases. The existing ones are meant to never change.

variables.doc_text: The connection identifier last used by the transfer. The connection id is unique number among all connections using the same connection cache. (Added in 8.2.0)
variables.name: conn_id

variables.doc_text: The Content-Type of the requested document, if there was any.
variables.name: content_type

variables.doc_text: The error message. (Added in 7.75.0)
variables.name: errormsg
variables.reads_source: if(per_result) { strinfo = per->errorbuffer[0] ? per->errorbuffer : curl_easy_strerror(per_result); valid = TRUE; }

variables.doc_text: The numerical exit code of the transfer. (Added in 7.75.0)
variables.name: exitcode
variables.reads_source: longinfo = (long)per_result; valid = TRUE;

variables.doc_text: The ultimate filename that curl writes out to. This is only meaningful if curl is told to write to a file with the --remote-name or --output option. It is most useful in combination with the --remote-header-name option. (Added in 7.26.0)
variables.name: filename_effective
variables.reads_source: if(per->outs.filename) { strinfo = per->outs.filename; valid = TRUE; }

variables.doc_text: The initial path curl ended up in when logging on to the remote FTP server. (Added in 7.15.4)
variables.name: ftp_entry_path

variables.doc_text: A JSON object with all HTTP response headers from the recent transfer. Values are provided as arrays, since in the case of multiple headers there can be multiple values. (Added in 7.83.0) The header names provided in lowercase, listed in order of appearance over the wire. Except for duplicated headers. They are grouped on the first occurrence of that header, each value is presented in the JSON array.
variables.name: header_json
variables.reads_source: headerJSON(stream, per);

variables.doc_text: The numerical response code that was found in the last retrieved HTTP(S) or FTP(s) transfer.
variables.name: http_code

variables.doc_text: The numerical code that was found in the last response (from a proxy) to a curl CONNECT request. (Added in 7.12.4)
variables.name: http_connect

variables.doc_text: The http version that was effectively used. (Added in 7.50.0)
variables.name: http_version

variables.doc_text: A JSON object with all available keys except `header_json`. (Added in 7.70.0)
variables.name: json
variables.reads_source: ourWriteOutJSON(stream, variables, CURL_ARRAYSIZE(variables), per, per_result);

variables.doc_text: The IP address of the local end of the most recently done connection - can be either IPv4 or IPv6. (Added in 7.29.0)
variables.name: local_ip

variables.doc_text: The local port number of the most recently done connection. (Added in 7.29.0)
variables.name: local_port

variables.doc_text: The http method used in the most recent HTTP request. (Added in 7.72.0)
variables.name: method

variables.doc_text: Number of server certificates received in the TLS handshake. Supported only by the OpenSSL, GnuTLS, Schannel and Rustls backends. (Added in 7.88.0)
variables.name: num_certs
variables.reads_source: certinfo(per); longinfo = per->certinfo ? per->certinfo->num_of_certs : 0; valid = TRUE;

variables.doc_text: Number of new connects made in the recent transfer. (Added in 7.12.3)
variables.name: num_connects

variables.doc_text: The number of response headers in the most recent request (restarted at each redirect). Note that the status line IS NOT a header. (Added in 7.73.0)
variables.name: num_headers
variables.reads_source: longinfo = per->num_headers; valid = TRUE;

variables.doc_text: Number of redirects that were followed in the request. (Added in 7.12.3)
variables.name: num_redirects

variables.doc_text: Number of retries actually performed when `--retry` has been used. (Added in 8.9.0)
variables.name: num_retries
variables.reads_source: longinfo = per->num_retries; valid = TRUE;

variables.doc_text: The rest of the output is only shown if the transfer returned a non-zero error. (Added in 7.75.0)
variables.name: onerror
variables.reads_source: if(per_result == CURLE_OK) /* this is not error so skip the rest */ done = TRUE;

variables.doc_text: The result of the HTTPS proxy's SSL peer certificate verification that was requested. 0 means the verification was successful. (Added in 7.52.0)
variables.name: proxy_ssl_verify_result

variables.doc_text: Returns 1 if the previous transfer used a proxy, otherwise 0. Useful for example to determine if a `NOPROXY` pattern matched the hostname or not. (Added in 8.7.0)
variables.name: proxy_used

variables.doc_text: When an HTTP request was made without --location to follow redirects (or when --max-redirs is met), this variable shows the actual URL a redirect *would* have gone to. (Added in 7.18.2)
variables.name: redirect_url

variables.doc_text: The Referer: header, if there was any. (Added in 7.76.0)
variables.name: referer

variables.doc_text: The remote IP address of the most recently done connection - can be either IPv4 or IPv6. (Added in 7.29.0)
variables.name: remote_ip

variables.doc_text: The remote port number of the most recently done connection. (Added in 7.29.0)
variables.name: remote_port

variables.doc_text: The numerical response code that was found in the last transfer (formerly known as "http_code"). (Added in 7.18.2)
variables.name: response_code

variables.doc_text: The URL scheme (sometimes called protocol) that was effectively used. (Added in 7.52.0)
variables.name: scheme

variables.doc_text: The total amount of data that were saved or written to stdout. When --compressed is used, this is likely different than `size_download`. Includes the headers in the count if --include is used.
variables.name: size_delivered

variables.doc_text: The total amount of bytes that were downloaded. This is the size of the body/data that was transferred, excluding headers.
variables.name: size_download

variables.doc_text: The total amount of bytes of the downloaded headers, as represented in HTTP/1-style header format.
variables.name: size_header

variables.doc_text: The total amount of bytes that were sent in the HTTP request.
variables.name: size_request

variables.doc_text: The total amount of bytes that were uploaded. This is the size of the body/data that was transferred, excluding headers.
variables.name: size_upload

variables.doc_text: The average download speed that curl measured for the complete download. Bytes per second.
variables.name: speed_download

variables.doc_text: The average upload speed that curl measured for the complete upload. Bytes per second.
variables.name: speed_upload

variables.doc_text: The result of the SSL peer certificate verification that was requested. 0 means the verification was successful. (Added in 7.19.0)
variables.name: ssl_verify_result

variables.doc_text: From this point on, the --write-out output is written to standard error. (Added in 7.63.0)
variables.name: stderr
variables.reads_source: if(fclose_stream) curlx_fclose(stream); fclose_stream = FALSE; stream = tool_stderr;

variables.doc_text: From this point on, the --write-out output is written to standard output. This is the default, but can be used to switch back after switching to stderr. (Added in 7.63.0)
variables.name: stdout
variables.reads_source: if(fclose_stream) curlx_fclose(stream); fclose_stream = FALSE; stream = stdout;

variables.doc_text: The time, in seconds, it took from the start until the SSL/SSH/etc connect/handshake to the remote host was completed. (Added in 7.19.0)
variables.name: time_appconnect

variables.doc_text: The time, in seconds, it took from the start until the TCP connect to the remote host (or proxy) was completed.
variables.name: time_connect

variables.doc_text: The time, in seconds, it took from the start until the name resolving was completed.
variables.name: time_namelookup

variables.doc_text: The time, in seconds, it took from the start until the last byte is sent by libcurl. (Added in 8.10.0)
variables.name: time_posttransfer

variables.doc_text: The time, in seconds, it took from the start until immediately before the file transfer was about to begin. This includes all pre-transfer commands and negotiations that are specific to the particular protocol(s) involved.
variables.name: time_pretransfer

variables.doc_text: The time, in seconds, the transfer was queued during its run. This adds the queue time for each redirect step that may have happened. Transfers may be queued for significant amounts of time when connection or parallel limits are in place. (Added in 8.12.0)
variables.name: time_queue

variables.doc_text: The time, in seconds, it took for all redirection steps including name lookup, connect, pretransfer and transfer before the final transaction was started. `time_redirect` shows the complete execution time for multiple redirections. (Added in 7.12.3)
variables.name: time_redirect

variables.doc_text: The time, in seconds, it took from the start until the first byte was received. This includes time_pretransfer and also the time the server needed to calculate the result.
variables.name: time_starttransfer

variables.doc_text: The total time, in seconds, that the full operation lasted.
variables.name: time_total

variables.doc_text: The amount of bytes that were sent as TLSv1.3 early data. This is 0 if this TLS feature was not used and negative if the data sent had been rejected by the server. The use of early data is enabled via the command line option `--tls-earlydata`. (Added in 8.13.0)
